rationale: Division game at home gives Seattle the edge despite both teams being inconsistent; Seahawks showed they can win big (20-3 vs KC) and home field matters in a coin-flip divisional matchup.
This is the game of the week with two 6-1 teams; Buffalo has been dominant recently (36-10 vs BAL) and their offense is elite, giving them a slight edge even in Minnesota.
Cincinnati at 5-2 is playing strong football with wins over BAL and TEN recently, while Atlanta was shut out 0-16 last week and has been inconsistent all season.
Cleveland at 5-3 has a better record and defense (held BAL to 10 points), while New Orleans at 2-5 has been struggling; CLE should handle a weak Saints team on the road.
Indianapolis at 2-6 has lost four straight and was blown out 7-42 last week; Dallas despite inconsistency should handle a Colts team in freefall.
Denver at 6-2 is on a four-game winning streak and playing elite football, while Carolina has lost two straight including a 43-13 blowout; Broncos are the clear class here.
Detroit at 5-2 is a legitimate contender and Miami at 1-6 is one of the worst teams in the league; Lions should win comfortably even on the road.
Both teams are 5-3 but New England has home field and has been playing well (45-17 vs LV, 26-19 vs NYJ); slight edge to the Patriots at home in a close matchup.
Los Angeles Chargers are 0-7 and winless on the season; Houston despite being 2-5 should be able to beat the worst team in the league.
Baltimore is without both QBs (Lamar Jackson out, Tyler Huntley out), making them essentially unwinnable at the position; JAX at 5-2 should dominate a QB-less Ravens squad.
The Rams at 4-4 have won two straight including a convincing 24-9 win over LAC, while Washington at 2-4 has been inconsistent; LA's talent edge tips this slightly.
San Francisco at 6-1 is one of the best teams in the NFC and playing at home; Las Vegas has lost three of four and lacks the talent to compete with the 49ers.
Philadelphia at 2-6 has lost four straight and looks like one of the worst teams in the NFC East; New York at 4-2 should handle their division rival convincingly.
Kansas City at 5-2 at home against a 2-6 Jets team that has been inconsistent all season; Chiefs should win comfortably at Arrowhead.
Chicago at 6-2 is one of the surprise teams of the season with three straight wins, while Tampa Bay at 3-5 has been inconsistent; Bears at home should prevail.
